s1.syndrome_frame: febrile neutropenic patient with cutaneous lesions and evidence of disseminated infection
salient_findings: vesicles with erythematous base on the skin
filamentous bacilli with septa on microscopic examination
key_facts: female infant with history of acute lymphoblastic leukemia
admitted for reinduction chemotherapy
became febrile 17 days after last day of chemotherapy
neutropenic at the time of fever
had an indwelling catheter
vesicles observed on the lower back and left thigh
tissue and blood cultures were obtained
punch biopsy of vesicle on lower back was performed
microscopic examination showed focal epidermal and subepidermal necrosis
numerous filamentous bacilli with septa on microscopic examination
gram stain revealed numerous gram-variable rods
periodic acid-Schiff staining was negative for fungal elements
PCR testing for HSV and VZV were negative
CT scan showed lesions in the liver and brain

shortlist.label: Bacillus cereus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Gram stain revealed numerous gram-variable rods and microscopic examination showed focal epidermal and subepidermal necrosis with numerous filamentous bacilli with septa, consistent with Bacillus cereus infection

shortlist.label: Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had an indwelling catheter and was neutropenic, increasing the risk for Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection, and the presence of cutaneous lesions is consistent with ecthyma gangrenosum, a characteristic skin lesion of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection

shortlist.label: Ecthyma gangrenosum
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with cutaneous lesions, and the presence of gram-negative rods on Gram stain is consistent with ecthyma gangrenosum, a characteristic skin lesion of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection

shortlist.label: Nocardia infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient was immunocompromised and had cutaneous lesions, increasing the risk for Nocardia infection, and the presence of filamentous bacilli with septa on microscopic examination is consistent with Nocardia infection

shortlist.label: Staphylococcus aureus infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had an indwelling catheter, increasing the risk for Staphylococcus aureus infection, and the presence of cutaneous lesions is consistent with Staphylococcus aureus infection

raw.rationale: The presence of vesicles with an erythematous base, focal epidermal and subepidermal necrosis, and gram-variable rods on microscopic examination, along with the patient's neutropenic state and history of indwelling catheter, are consistent with Ecthyma gangrenosum, a characteristic skin lesion of Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection, particularly in immunocompromised patients.

rejected.label: Bacillus cereus infection
rejected.why: While Bacillus cereus can cause infections in immunocompromised patients, the clinical presentation and microscopic findings do not specifically point towards this organism.

rejected.label: Pseudomonas aeruginosa infection
rejected.why: Although Pseudomonas aeruginosa is the causative agent of Ecthyma gangrenosum, the shortlist item 'Ecthyma gangrenosum' more specifically describes the condition presented in the vignette.

rejected.label: Nocardia infection
rejected.why: Nocardia infections typically present with abscesses or cellulitis and are more commonly associated with filamentous, branching gram-positive rods, which does not match the gram-variable rods described in the vignette.

rejected.label: Staphylococcus aureus infection
rejected.why: The microscopic examination showing gram-variable rods and the clinical context do not support Staphylococcus aureus as the primary cause, as this organism typically appears as gram-positive cocci in clusters.
